text: In the two-state (ON/OFF) promoter model of bursty gene expression, a high koff/kon ratio (promoter mostly OFF) leads to:
choices: A Fano factor close to 1 (Poisson-like mRNA statistics)
A perfectly deterministic mRNA level with zero variance
Negative mRNA copy numbers, which is biologically meaningless
A Fano factor greater than 1 (super-Poissonian, 'bursty' mRNA statistics)
explanation: When koff/kon is high, the promoter spends most of its time OFF and only occasionally switches ON to fire off bursts of transcription, producing super-Poissonian variance and a Fano factor greater than 1. A Fano factor near 1 instead corresponds to the opposite regime (low koff/kon, promoter mostly ON, more Poisson-like firing); mRNA counts are never negative or noise-free in this stochastic model.
